newsitem.title: ECUADOR: SOCCER-CHILE GAIN PRIZE POINT IN ECUADOR.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CHILE GAIN PRIZE POINT IN ECUADOR.

text.p: Chile overcame the absence of top striker Ivan Zamorano and the Quito altitude to pick up a valuable away point as they drew 1-1 with Ecuador in a World Cup qualifier on Sunday.

Argentine-born striker Ariel Graziani headed Ecuador ahead one minute before halftime but Chile hit back in the 54th minute when Marcelo Salas, who plays for Argentine champions River Plate, scored with a spectacular header.

Chile, whose last appearance at the World Cup finals was in 1982, have 13 points from 10 games in the single South American group. But they play five of their six remaining games at home, where they have a 100 percent record to date.

Ecuador, who have never reachwed the World Cup finals, have 14 points from 11 games, but play three of their remaining games away, where their form has been poor. Four of the nine countries qualify for France.
Ecuador, with the advantage of playing at 2,800 metres above sea level, created more chances but lacked firepower in attack.
Zamorano, who scored five goals as Chile beat Venezuela 6-0 in April, was suspended on two yellow cards.

Ecuador - Geovany Ibarra, Ivan Hurtado, Ulises de la Cruz, Alberto Montano, Edmundo Mendez, Marco Constante, Jimmy Blandin, Oswaldo de la Cruz (Eduardo Hurtado, 60), Alex Aguinaga, Agustin Delgado (Gilson de Souza, 60), Ariel Graziani (Angel Fernndez, 65).

Chile - Marcelo Ramirez, Cristian Castaneda, Javier Margas, Carlos Gonzalez, Marcelo Miranda, Luis Musri, (Fernando Cornejo, 57), Clarence Acuna, Pedro Reyes, Jose Luis Sierra (Jaime Rivero, 71), Pedro Gonzalez (Claudio Nunez, 52), Marcelo Salas.
